postTitle: Is 0% EMI or Buy Now Pay Later Really Free? When Free Is Free
topic: 0% instalments charge no interest, so who pays? Often the shop; and no interest does not always mean the lowest price

assumptions.notes: Lesson: when a plan charges nothing, the cost lands elsewhere: the shop pays a fee (it sells more), the price is higher, or a cash discount is lost (Jiri: €1,200 in instalments or €1,140 paid now; €60, about 10% a year, left in the lesson). Free when the price is the same, no fees, every payment on time. Numbers: 0%, €1,200, €1,140.

caption.instagram:
Instalments with no interest. Who pays for that?

Often the shop pays the company behind the plan a fee, because instalments help it sell more. But no interest does not always mean the lowest price. Imagine a laptop at €1,200 in instalments, or €1,140 paid now: no interest, and it still costs more.

The price for paying now shows the difference. Same price, no fees, every payment on time: then it can cost you nothing extra.
